subject: [r-inla] Failure of spatio-temporal modeling based on binomial

messages.author: 92737d96d07e78d4
messages.subject: [r-inla] Failure of spatio-temporal modeling based on binomial
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am fitting a spatio-temporal additive model with covariates using negative binomial likelihood to a large count data (n>36000 records). The code works fine without any issue in R version 4.31., R-INLA 23.08.08 under windows 10 x64. 
# ###### formula and INLA commands used ######:
lcar.iid.ad <- O ~ f(ID.area, model="generic1", Cmatrix=Q_Leroux, constr=TRUE,         hyper=list(prec=list(prior=sdunif),beta=list(prior=lunif))) +
            f(ID.month, model="iid", constr=TRUE, hyper=list(theta=list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.01)))) + X1 + X2 + X3 + X4 + X5 + X6 + X7 + X8

model_lcar.iid.ad<-INLA::inla(lcar.iid.ad, family="nbinomial", data=Data.INLA, E=E, control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE, link=1,cdf=c(log(1))), control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE, waic=TRUE), control.inla=list(strategy="simplified.laplace", npoints=21),verbose=TRUE)

Recently, I have switched over to a new laptop MacPro M2 and tried running the same code using R version 4.3.1 (2023-06-16), under: macOS Ventura 13.4.1, and R-INLA version 23.08.08. After several function evaluations, it crashed with the following error:

Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  *** Failed to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.

 I would request you all to kindly help me in resolving this issue.

Thanks in advance
S. Subramanian
